title: Eliminate Maximum Number of Monsters
summary: In a video game, you defend a city from n monsters moving towards it.
statement: In a video game, you defend a city from n monsters moving towards it. Each monster's initial distance and speed are given. You have a weapon that can eliminate one monster per minute, charging in one minute. Monsters move at a constant speed. Return the maximum number of monsters you can eliminate before any reach the city, or n if all can be eliminated.
constraints: The equal-length arrays contain 1 through 100000 positive values.
One monster may be eliminated at minute 0 and one more at each later integer minute.
The game ends before firing when any living monster reaches the city.
hints: Convert each monster to the last integer minute when it can safely be shot: floor((distance-1)/speed).
Sort these deadlines and schedule one shot per minute in earliest-deadline order.
Stop when the next deadline is earlier than its assigned minute.
Earliest-deadline scheduling is optimal by exchange: swapping an earlier deadline ahead never makes either shot less feasible.
editorial: Earliest-deadline scheduling is optimal by exchange: swapping an earlier deadline ahead never makes either shot less feasible.

tests.explanation: The monsters reach at minutes one, three, and four, so all three can be eliminated first.
Two monsters arrive at minute one; after the minute-zero shot, another reaches the city, so only one is eliminated.
